title: WHY JUST LOOK AT EACH OTHER?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, 'Why do you just keep looking at each other?' He continued, 'I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die.'" - Gen 42:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The famine has reached Canaan, and Jacob's family is in danger of starving. Yet his sons seem frozen, doing nothing — "just looking at each other," paralyzed perhaps by fear or indecision. So Jacob rouses them: there is grain in Egypt; go and buy it, "so that we may live and not die." He calls his sons out of passivity and into action.

Sometimes, in the face of a problem, we too "just keep looking at each other" — talking about it, worrying over it, waiting for someone else to move — while doing nothing. Fear and uncertainty can leave us stuck, staring at a difficulty instead of taking the step that would help.

But notice: the grain was available in Egypt; provision was there. The family would not be saved by staring at their empty barns, but by getting up and going to where the provision was. God had made a way — through Joseph's storehouses, as we know — but they had to act to receive it.

Is there a situation where you have been passive when you should be moving? God often provides, but He also calls us to get up and go take hold of what He has made available. Do not let fear keep you frozen. Take the step of faith in front of you. Provision is there; go and receive it, so that you may "live and not die."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I "just looking" at a problem instead of acting?
2. Has fear or uncertainty left me frozen when I should move?
3. What step of faith is God calling me to take today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when fear leaves me frozen before a problem, stir me to action. Give me courage to get up and go take hold of the provision You have made. Help me to move in faith. Amen.
